People often use "i.e." when they mean "e.g.", or "e.g." when they mean "i.e." It's similar to when people use long words to sound smart -- if you use it wrong, you look more foolish than if you had just spoken plainly.

"I.e." and "e.g." are really useful though, so you should learn when to use them:

  • i.e. means "that is", or "in other words". It stands for id est ("it is").

The Voat goat, i.e., the cute animal that shows up when Voat is down, is a silly mascot.

  • e.g. means "for example" (exempli gratia), and is used with short lists or a single example, e.g.:

Other sites also have silly mascots (e.g., Reddit's alien, Hipmunk's chipmunk, Evernot's elephant).

Note that both i.e. and e.g. can be used parenthetically or offset by commas.

Another helpful resource is this The Oatmeal comic/infographic.
